headword: {勧善懲悪|かんぜんちょうあく}
gloss: rewarding good and punishing evil; poetic justice

definitions.gloss: rewarding good and punishing evil; poetic justice
definitions.explanation: A moral principle and narrative theme in which good deeds are rewarded and evil deeds are punished. Commonly used to describe stories, dramas, and cultural works that follow this clear-cut moral framework.

examples.japanese: {勧善懲悪|かんぜんちょうあく}の{物語|ものがたり}。
examples.english: A story of good triumphing over evil.

examples.japanese: {時代劇|じだいげき}は{勧善懲悪|かんぜんちょうあく}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: Period dramas often feature good-versus-evil storylines.

examples.japanese: {子供向|こどもむ}けのアニメは{勧善懲悪|かんぜんちょうあく}の{構造|こうぞう}がはっきりしている。
examples.english: Children's anime have a clear good-versus-evil structure.

notes:
A four-character compound ({四字熟語|よじじゅくご}): {勧|かん} (encourage) + {善|ぜん} (good) + {懲|ちょう} (punish) + {悪|あく} (evil). This is one of the foundational moral themes in East Asian literature and drama.

CULTURAL CONTEXT:
This concept is central to traditional Japanese storytelling. Period dramas ({時代劇|じだいげき}) like {水戸黄門|みとこうもん} and {遠山|とおやま}の{金|きん}さん are classic examples — the hero always defeats the villain and justice prevails. Modern usage sometimes carries a slightly dismissive tone, implying the story is simplistic or predictable.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {勧善懲悪|かんぜんちょうあく}の{物語|ものがたり} — a good-versus-evil story
- {勧善懲悪|かんぜんちょうあく}もの — a work with a good-vs-evil theme
- {勧善懲悪|かんぜんちょうあく}の{精神|せいしん} — the spirit of rewarding good and punishing evil

RELATED TERMS:
- {因果応報|いんがおうほう} — karmic retribution; what goes around comes around
- {自業自得|じごうじとく} — reaping what you sow; getting what you deserve
- {正義|せいぎ} — justice; righteousness
